# How values that overlap are resolved, and which pattern the redaction is
# attributed to.
#
# No built-in pattern states these rules. Two of them do overlap, and one value
# does contain another — a stateless installation token carries a JWT, and the
# signature of a JWT swallows a token written after it — but no input makes two
# of them start together or cover the same span, so the rules that decide
# attribution when they do, the longest and then the one added first, have no
# built-in input at all. The patterns here look for a given substring instead,
# so that the input a case is written against can be read at a glance rather
# than decoded. The letters say where the values are; nothing about them is a
# credential.
#
# Values that overlap are redacted together as one, and the combined text is
# attributed to the pattern that located the value starting earliest; among
# those, the longest; among those, the one added first.

patterns: earlier-and-later

case: values that overlap are redacted as one
in:   xxabcdefxx
out:  xx«early»xx

case: values that do not overlap stay apart
in:   abcdxxcdef
out:  «early»xx«late»

case: patterns that find nothing
in:   nothing here at all
out:  nothing here at all

patterns: earlier-and-later-reversed

case: the earlier value is attributed however the patterns were ordered
in:   xxabcdefxx
out:  xx«early»xx

patterns: same-start

case: on the same start the longest value is attributed
in:   abcdefxx
out:  «long»efxx

patterns: same-start-reversed

case: on the same start the longest is attributed however the patterns were ordered
in:   abcdefxx
out:  «long»efxx

patterns: same-span

case: on the same span the pattern added first is attributed
in:   abcdxx
out:  «first»xx

patterns: same-span-reversed

case: on the same span the order of the patterns decides, not the name
in:   abcdxx
out:  «second»xx

patterns: containing

case: a value inside another is redacted as part of it
in:   abcdef
out:  «outer»

patterns: containing-reversed

case: a value inside another is attributed to the containing one whatever the order
in:   abcdef
out:  «outer»

patterns: chained

case: a chain of overlaps merges into one value
in:   abcdefg
out:  «first»

case: a chain that stops short leaves the rest alone
in:   abcxxefgxx
out:  «first»xx«third»xx

patterns: adjacent

case: values that touch but do not overlap stay apart
in:   abcd
out:  «first»«second»

case: touching values twice over
in:   abcdabcd
out:  «first»«second»«first»«second»
